subject: Egypt
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about the Nile. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). The river is drawn as an approximate route through places named in the article, not traced from map data. Sudan has a flagged area in the map data (Abyei), which this episode does not show, so it needs the borders review before release.

claims.text: The Nile is a major north-flowing river in northeast Africa which empties into the Mediterranean Sea.
At 7,088 kilometres long, it is the longest river in the world.
The White Nile begins near Lake Victoria and flows through Uganda and South Sudan.
The Blue Nile begins near Lake Tana in Ethiopia and flows into Sudan from the southeast.
The two rivers meet at the Sudanese capital, Khartoum.
The Nile’s drainage basin extends across eleven countries.

victoria.note: Lake Victoria, near where the White Nile begins.

tana.note: Lake Tana, where the Blue Nile begins.

khartoum.note: Khartoum, where the two rivers meet.

delta.note: Where the Nile empties into the Mediterranean.
